title: How would you estimate how many car tyres are sold in the UK each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many car tyres are sold in the UK each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: The UK buys roughly 34 million replacement car tyres a year: about 34 million cars, four tyres each, replaced on average every four years. Add tyres fitted to new cars at the factory and the total is nearer 42 million. This is a replacement-cycle question, a pattern you will reuse for phones, laptops, chairs and anything else people buy again every few years. Try your own estimate before you read on.
body:
The question

How many car tyres are sold in the UK each year?

The structure is short: cars × tyres per car ÷ years a tyre lasts. The judgement is in defining the market (replacement tyres or all tyres, cars only or vans too) and in defending how long a tyre lasts.

Clarify before you calculate

  • Replacement or all tyres? Most tyre cases are about the replacement market, sold through garages and fitting centres. Tyres fitted to new cars at the factory ("original equipment") are a separate channel. Size replacement first, then add new cars if asked.
  • Which vehicles? Cars only. Vans, lorries and motorbikes use different tyres.
  • Units or value? Units per year.

Rough guess: "Tens of millions. Roughly one tyre per car per year."

Step by step

  1. Cars on UK roads: 34M. The Department for Transport counted about 34.0M licensed cars at the end of 2024.
  2. Tyres per car: 4 → 34M × 4 = 136M tyres in use.
  3. Average life of a tyre: 4 years. A typical car covers about 7,000 miles a year and a tyre lasts roughly 28,000 miles, so 28,000 ÷ 7,000 = 4 years.
  4. Replacement tyres a year: 136M ÷ 4 = 34M.

That is about one tyre per car per year, which fits the common pattern of replacing a pair every couple of years.

Source for the car count: DfT: Vehicle licensing statistics, UK 2024.

Sanity check from a second angle

Size it from the sellers' side. Assume about 10,000 places fit tyres (fast-fit centres, independent garages, dealers and mobile fitters), each fitting 12 tyres a day over 300 working days: 10,000 × 12 × 300 = 36M tyres. That lands within 6% of the demand-side answer.

An industry anchor helps too. The Tyre Industry Federation once estimated the UK replacement car tyre market (including 4x4 and light van tyres) at more than 30M units a year. That figure dates from 2009, and the car fleet has grown since, but it confirms the order of magnitude.

Which assumption matters most

Tyre life, not the car count. The number of cars is published and stable. Tyre life varies widely: a low-mileage car may keep its tyres for six years, while a minicab doing 25,000 miles a year needs new ones every year or so. If the average life is five years instead of four, the answer becomes 136M ÷ 5 = 27.2M, 20% lower.

A refined estimate would segment private cars and high-mileage vehicles (taxis, fleet cars, delivery cars), each with its own replacement cycle. You might also mention punctures and damage, which add replacements regardless of wear.

Add tyres on new cars if asked

About 2.0M new cars were registered in the UK in 2024 (DfT). At four tyres each, that is about 8M original-equipment tyres. Total tyres: 34M + 8M = about 42M. Keep the two channels separate, because they have different buyers (motorists versus car makers) and very different prices.

What a strong answer sounds like

"I'll size the replacement market first. About 34 million cars with four tyres each is 136 million tyres on the road. A tyre lasts about 28,000 miles and the average car does about 7,000 a year, so four years. That's roughly 34 million replacement tyres a year. From the supply side, 10,000 fitters doing 12 a day gets me to a similar number. Tyre life is the sensitive assumption: at five years it's about 27 million."

A weak answer says "34 million cars, everyone buys four tyres a year, so 136 million". It confuses the tyres in use (the stock) with the tyres bought each year (the flow).

Common mistakes

  • Stock versus flow. Divide the tyres in use by their life to get annual sales.
  • Mixing channels. Factory-fitted and replacement tyres are different markets. Ask which one the client cares about.
  • Assuming all four tyres are replaced together. Front tyres often wear faster. The average-life method handles this, so long as you think of it per tyre.

Practice

1. What is the UK replacement car tyre market worth?

Show the answer

34M tyres × an average of $120 fitted = about $4.1B a year. Clarify whether the price includes fitting, balancing and disposal, which some retailers charge separately.

2. Suppose electric cars wear tyres 20% faster and make up 10% of cars. How much does that add to annual demand?

Show the answer

3.4M EVs × 4 tyres = 13.6M tyres. Their life falls from 4 years to 4 ÷ 1.2 = 3.33 years, so they need 13.6M ÷ 3.33 = about 4.1M tyres a year instead of 3.4M. That adds about 0.7M, only 2% of the market, but growing as EVs spread.

Where to practise next

Use the same replacement logic on UK office chairs and smartphones in India. For the general method, read how to answer a market sizing question step by step, and for buyers' side versus sellers' side checks, see this quick tip.
